canonicalPersonas.mergeEvidence: RE-EVALUATED AGAINST THE ADMINISTRATION SURFACE, not inherited. ADMIN_MUTATION_OPERATIONS is gated by requireAdministrationAuthority(actor.heldRoleKeys, action) over the closed action set editObjectDefinition | editRoleDefinition | editWorkflowDefinition | assignRole. The first three require the Role KEY `admin` (ADMIN_ROLE_KEY) and nothing else; assignRole permits owner | generalManager | admin. The owner-executive persona holds `admin` in nonprod (measured). A second Principal holding `admin` would produce byte-identical answers on all 19 mutations and all 13 reads. The difference would be org-chart position, which is a Job Role, not an authority.
canonicalPersonas.whatWouldSeparateThem: A persona holding `owner` but NOT `admin`. That persona is measurably different -- it would be REFUSED editObjectDefinition, editRoleDefinition and editWorkflowDefinition while still holding admin.employeeWorkEligibility.write and admin.employeeOperationalScope.write, because those two are capability-gated and the Administration definition surface is Role-key-gated. The catalog contains no such persona. That, not 'Administrator', is the genuinely missing administrative persona.

CONFIRMS THE INHERITED FINDING. POST /admin/policy serves 13 ADMIN_READ_OPERATIONS (listTenantPrincipals, listObjects, readObjectWithFields, listRoles, readRolePolicy, listPrincipalRoleAssignments, listObjectsWithActions, getObjectSecurityMatrix, getRoleSecurity, getPrincipalEffectiveAccess, listWorkflows, readWorkflowVersion, readPolicyAuditHistory) and 19 ADMIN_MUTATION_OPERATIONS, over the Firebase-verified bearer token. Reads require only an active Principal with an ACTIVE tenant membership -- so every one of the 15 personas can perform them. Mutations are gated on ROLE KEYS: editObjectDefinition / editRoleDefinition / editWorkflowDefinition require `admin`; assignRole permits owner | generalManager | admin. owner-executive holds `admin` in nonprod (measured).
